correctness.rationale: The quotient multiplication gives independent vertex equations a_v b_v=0 and arrow equations a_u s_alpha+r_alpha b_v=0. Expansion by selected arrow constraints yields the exact positive weighted subgraph identity. Each selected-incident vertex contributes q if pure and 1 if mixed; positivity gives the bipartite maximum and the two-arrow witness proves strictness. On paths the selected-edge runs have endpoint factors fixed by F; every internal vertex contributes 1 at a directed passage and q at a turn, yielding both sharp and unique extrema. The two transfer matrices have the displayed characteristic quadratics; Cayley–Hamilton yields the recurrences with verified n=0,1,2 boundaries. Their plus roots dominate and P_U(lambda_L+)=(q-1)^2(2q-1-lambda_L+)<0, so lambda_U+>lambda_L+. The standalone verify.py directly checks all small algebra multiplications and independent subgraph counts, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The zero-product probability is a standard ring invariant and orientation affects actual multiplication in otherwise equally sized path algebras. The theorem gives a natural complete classification of both extrema for every path and all maxima for every bipartite multigraph, rather than small examples or renaming a prior count. The exact exponential-rate gap quantitatively separates two canonical orientations in growing families; this motivation exists independently of the enumeration algorithm. Restriction to simple paths for minima is explicit and not an arbitrary field/dimension slice.
